summary: The Consumer Fuel Costs Relief Act temporarily eliminates federal taxes on motor and aviation fuels until October 1, 2027. To prevent a loss of funding for public infrastructure, the bill requires the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer equivalent amounts from the general fund of the Treasury to the Highway Trust Fund and the Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund. It also sets a policy that the tax savings must be passed directly on to consumers through lower prices, directing federal agencies to enforce this policy and monitor markets for price gouging.

affected_groups.effect: Expected to receive the financial benefits of the tax holiday through reduced prices for transportation motor fuels and aviation services.
affected_groups.group: Consumers of motor and aviation fuels

affected_groups.effect: Must lower fuel prices to reflect the tax reduction and face monetary penalties if they fail to pass savings on to consumers.
affected_groups.group: Transportation motor fuels producers and dealers

affected_groups.effect: Must ensure passengers immediately receive the benefits of the tax reduction and face monetary penalties if they fail to do so.
affected_groups.group: Aviation gasoline producers and airline service providers

affected_groups.effect: Required to execute trust fund transfers, ensure consumers receive tax reduction benefits, and monitor markets for price gouging and manipulation.

key_provisions: Sets the tax rates under section 4081(a)(2)(A) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to zero for taxable fuel removed, entered, or sold between the date of enactment and October 1, 2027.
Exempts taxable fuel from the Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund financing rate during the same period.
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer funds from the general fund to the Highway Trust Fund and the Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund to make up for the reduced tax revenues.

Establishes a congressional policy that transportation motor fuels producers, dealers, and airline service providers must immediately pass the tax reduction benefits on to consumers through lower prices.
Subject fuel producers, airline service providers, and dealers who fail to pass on the price reductions to monetary penalties at least equal to the unpassed tax reduction amount.
Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to monitor oil, diesel, and gasoline markets to prevent price gouging and market manipulation.
missing_information: Specific numerical dollar values for the tax rates being eliminated.
Specific penalty amounts for entities that fail to pass tax savings on to consumers, other than that they must not be less than the unpassed tax reduction amount.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Consumer Fuel Costs Relief Act temporarily eliminates federal taxes on motor and aviation fuels until October 1, 2027. To prevent a loss of funding for public infrastructure, the bill requires the Secretary of the Treasury to transfer equivalent amounts from the general fund of the Treasury to the Highway Trust Fund and the Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund. It also sets a policy that the tax savings must be passed directly on to consumers through lower prices, directing federal agencies to enforce this policy and monitor markets for price gouging.
summary_detail.significance: The bill temporarily alters federal tax policy regarding motor and aviation fuels by reducing tax rates to zero through September 2027 while maintaining trust fund revenues via general fund transfers. It also creates a federal enforcement mechanism involving the Treasury, FTC, and CFTC to compel fuel producers and sellers to pass tax savings to consumers.
